## During the seminar

A field experiment motivates the difference-in-means estimator. We distinguish
an estimand, an estimator, and an estimate, then examine unbiasedness,
sampling variability, mean squared error, and consistency.

Potential outcomes help separate random assignment from random sampling and
explain why a comparison under self-selection can miss the average treatment
effect. Demos 1-4 prepare for B3, including exact enumeration of assignments,
repeated studies, and summaries and CDFs of their estimates.

The final slide sequence and Demos 5-7 are optional. They revisit estimated
standard errors, the exact t distribution under Normal observations, and
the large-sample Normal approximation.

## After class

**B3 is due October 21 at 1:30 p.m. Pacific.** Accept your private repository
invitation and follow its README. The hypothetical village data and helpers
are included. Complete the QMD's code and written responses, run the completion
check, and render a fresh HTML. Commit and push **both the QMD and current HTML**.

Keep track of what changes in each simulation: treatment assignment, sampled
villages, the number of villages per study, or the number of simulation
repetitions. These produce different kinds of variation.
